sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Library list with fixed versions
sections.what: Lists every library with one fixed version, grouped by purpose, with short comments for the database driver and OpenAI.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes each installation repeatable.
sections.watch_out: Do not upgrade one library alone, because newer versions can clash with the pinned versions around them.

summary: Lists the exact third-party libraries the backend needs, each with a fixed version number, so the installation is repeatable.
purpose: Lets someone install the same libraries the project was built with.
why: Likely reason: fixed versions prevent surprises when a library is updated.
how: 1. Groups the libraries by purpose: web framework, database, data checks, calculations, export, web scraping, AI and search, optional queue, testing, utilities, OpenAI and Tavily. 2. Each line fixes one version. 3. The installer reads the list and installs everything.
inputs: The file is read by pip, the Python installer.
outputs: A set of installed libraries in the Python environment.
risks: Several libraries are large or need system software (WeasyPrint, lxml, sentence-transformers, faiss-cpu, psycopg2). Optional services (psycopg2, redis, rq, openai) are installed along with required ones. Old pinned versions may have known security issues. Changing one line alone can cause version conflicts.
debug: If installation fails, read the first error line. Many failures come from WeasyPrint or lxml needing system libraries. Check that the Python version matches the project's requirement.
